title: Collab: validate/normalize inbound CRDT state before it hits FlashDocument (untrusted-peer hardening)
description: SECURITY + DATA-INTEGRITY gap found in QA review of collab P0/P1 (HEAD 6856134; binding e0b5c25, transport 769796c). The collab trust model is 'anyone with the share link is a full read/write collaborator' (Google-Docs-style) — opt-in/off-by-default is sound (verified: nothing in apps/ calls startCollab/joinCollab/attachCollab; solo opens NO network connection; the OpenRouter API key + signaling override live in localStorage, NOT in the FlashDocument, so collab does not sync secrets). The exposure is the INBOUND path: a peer's Y.Doc is rebuilt and applied to the LIVE model with ZERO validation. packages/collab/src/schema.ts rebuildDoc() casts the Y.Doc contents 'as unknown as FlashDocument' (line ~700); rebuildFields (ymap-fields.ts) copies whatever scalar values a peer put in each Y.Map entry; the authoring-ui binding (collabAdapter.storeAsDocSource.applyRemote) calls store.replaceDoc(rebuilt), and documentStore REPLACE sets it verbatim — no schema/shape/type check anywhere. CONSEQUENCES from a malicious OR buggy peer: (1) structurally-invalid doc (wrong types, missing required fields, non-array where the renderer/compiler expects an array, NaN coords, huge arrays) → can crash the editor render loop or the SWF compiler (DoS), or cause type-confusion. (2) peer-supplied AS2 frame scripts / asClasses sources are compiled+run on every collaborator's machine (script vector — inherent to the doc-sharing model, but worth an explicit threat-model note). (3) asClasses paths arrive UNvalidated: rebuildAsClasses keys by raw 'path' with no normalizeClassPath() gate, so a crafted path (.. / leading slash / NUL) could traverse when the joiner later syncs classes to the class VFS (WebClassVfs/TauriClassVfs disk mirror) — normalizeClassPath is the existing defense in @flash/core/vfs but the collab rebuild does not invoke it. SCOPE: add a validation/normalization layer on the INBOUND boundary (rebuildDoc result, before replaceDoc) — reject or sanitize malformed structures, clamp/validate types, run class paths through normalizeClassPath, and fail safe (keep last-good doc) rather than applying garbage. Also assess whether AS2/asClasses from a remote peer should require trust/confirmation. TEST GAP: the collab suite (9 P0 + 19 P1, all green) covers convergence thoroughly (7200-mutation property identity test, per-field/atomic-LWW/char-level concurrent merge, late-join, minimal-delta) but has NO malformed-update / malicious-CRDT test — add fuzz/adversarial cases that inject invalid Y.Doc state and assert the editor neither crashes nor adopts an invalid model. Relates to collab P5 hardening (1348) which covers transport/encryption but NOT inbound model validation. NOT yet wired to any UI (no apps/ caller), so this is pre-emptive hardening before P4 UX ships the share dialog.
